prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1346; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officers were dispatched to a two-vehicle collision on a residential roadway in Pearland, Texas, where a low-speed head-on impact had occurred between two passenger vehicles. Driver 1 and Driver 2 were both on scene, and a Passenger was confirmed to have been seated in the vehicle operated by Driver 1 at the time of impact. Officers spoke with Driver 2 and two independent witnesses, all of whom gave accounts consistent with the physical evidence and with the scene photographs taken on arrival. Driver 1 reported a shoulder injury, and the nature of the impact is consistent with that type of injury given the direction and force of the collision. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was known to any party or observed by officers. Officers noted that it is not clear whether all of the visible damage resulted from this single impact, and the question was left open for further review. Driver 1 is listed as a member of the policyholder's household and was identified as an authorized driver of the vehicle. Medical attention was offered at the scene, and both drivers were transported for evaluation.
